title: Enforce recovery at the universal mutation boundary
description:
Every mutating CLI path runs cache-free recovery dispatch before repository validation or command-layer configuration construction, and every later storage mutation remains guarded against races without reentrant recovery or lock-order violation.

## Background

Pending transaction state must be recoverable before partial repository state can prevent normal storage or command construction. The same config-independent coordinator covers CLI mutation entrypoints and the mutation-capable HTTP server startup path.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: CLI commands use one exhaustive mutability classification and the mutation-capable HTTP server uses the same coordinator at startup; before `storage.validate()` or any config/rules/gates/templates/schema cache, they locate `.jit-bootstrap/` or `.jit/`, recover external then internal journals, re-resolve root state, and only then construct normal services.
- [hard] REQ-02: The repository mutation guard still prevents a transaction appearing between entrypoint recovery and a write; an internal guarded path is the only recovery writer, with fixed bootstrap-before-repository-before-event lock order.
- [hard] REQ-03: Generated CLI-enumeration and server-startup tests fail for missing recovery dispatch, and fixtures prove partial/no-index fresh roots, invalid partial config/rules, prepared rollback, committed roll-forward, cleanup residue, concurrent mutation, init, explicit recover, and restored-to-no-repository behavior.

## Scope

**Blast radius:** CLI and HTTP-server startup/root discovery, CLI mutability classification, minimal recovery coordinator, repository mutation-guard contract, and mechanical adoption and tests for every writer family. This task consumes the existing transaction kernel and does not add profile command syntax.

**Green landing:** Existing mutations retain clean-repository behavior and deterministically recover pending journals before startup validation, cache construction, or target changes.
